Adding a couple of concrete artifacts for the meeting — see attached spreadsheet with two sizing scenarios (steady-state vs peak-burst) and a short notes sheet on isolation strategies (hard isolation by pool, soft isolation w/ QoS and token quotas).

A couple of pre-read highlights to save time on the call:
- If your tail-latency SLO is <200ms for 95th, we recommend reserving 40–50% of peak baseline in a hot pool and leaving a separate burst pool with capped runtime memory to handle short spikes.
- Autoscale policy: prefer a two-stage policy — fast incremental scale (add 1 slot at 60% queue for 30s) and a slower scaling window for large spikes (add up to 3 slots if sustained >3m).
- On isolation: hard isolation gives stronger security guarantees but increases unit cost; our soft-iso mode relies on GPU context partitioning + QoS and works well if tenants are trusted.

Attaching: pool-sizing-projections.xlsx (XLSX, 78KB)

—Marcus
